title: Shared compression library: runtime validation blocked
subtitle: codex (gpt-6) · line: xswap-compression-tiering · base 5e84ca92 · 1 candidate · 3 guests / 3 builds

verdict.headline: The library compiled, but a conflicting debug setup stopped runtime validation.

sections.title: A reusable engine, awaiting runtime evidence
sections.lead: The aim is to share compression and object storage while keeping the current swap policy and ownership. Independent XSwap and pressure-driven disk demotion are later phases.

blocks.text: Hypothesis: a common engine can serve another frontend without duplicating codec and storage cleanup. Source review gives high confidence in the boundary; runtime behavior remains untested.

Two baseline guests passed; one earlier baseline attempt remains infrastructure-invalid with an audited replacement. Three builds were charged: two valid baseline builds and one candidate image rejected by its required configuration gate.

sections.title: 1. Whole system: restore the application page
sections.lead: An application needs its full page in physical RAM. Stored contents may be compressed inside RAM or reside on a backing device. Compression trades CPU work for less storage traffic.

blocks.takeaway: The changed engine serves compressed contents inside RAM
blocks.note: Schematic path, with no illustrative size or timing used as a measurement.

blocks.text: The candidate changes the compressed-storage implementation. The existing frontend still decides admission, accounting and writeback. No new RAM-to-disk migration policy is implemented here.

sections.title: 2. Subsystem: policy keeps the object identity
sections.lead: ZSwap retains the entry index, memory-group charge, ordering and lifetime pins. A shared page library owns per-CPU codec contexts, scratch buffers and compressed-object storage.

blocks.takeaway: Data moves through the engine; policy stays with the frontend

blocks.text: Each successful store returns a handle and length. The caller publishes and accounts for that object, retains it across loads, and releases it after users drain. Failed compression leaves the raw-storage policy with ZSwap.

sections.title: 3. Concrete change: one explicit library boundary
sections.lead: The same page A and stored object A appear before and after. The extraction moves mechanism ownership; it does not remove compression work or change what is stored.

blocks.takeaway: Before: one frontend contains policy and engine
After: the frontend calls a shared engine

blocks.text: Source review found unchanged per-object entries and per-CPU context layout. A separate pool wrapper adds an allocation. Allocator footprint, call overhead and fault latency remain unmeasured.

Compilation passed. The frozen debug input enabled SLUB_TINY, which prevents the required KASAN memory checker. Configured coverage failed before any candidate guest, KUnit execution, sanitizer run, calibration or performance comparison.

sections.title: Measured results

blocks.text: No complete paired performance result is available.

sections.lead: High confidence in the recorded stopping cause; candidate behavior and costs remain unknown.

sections.title: Continue under a separately frozen correction
sections.lead: Preserve this closed contract and test the unchanged candidate only after correcting the debug input. Independent XSwap and tier migration stay behind successful C1 correctness coverage.

blocks.takeaway: Coverage must pass before measuring any benefit

blocks.text: The correction preserves the original resource ceiling and deadline. Ownership, accounting, cleanup, metadata or calibrated latency failures would falsify the candidate. This attempt provides no speed or equivalence result.

sections.title: Core kernel patches

blocks.takeaway: K1: the API keeps publication, accounting and handle lifetime with its caller
K1: the library compresses and allocates before returning a usable handle
K1: frontend pool creation delegates the engine and preserves its reference lifetime
